entry.name: Machine Learning Specialization
entry.note: Andrew Ng's rebuilt classic; the most common starting point in the field

covers: Python with NumPy, scikit-learn, and TensorFlow
reading.format: Three-course program delivered through video lessons that first give intuitive visual explanations, then step-by-step code walkthroughs, with optional videos covering the underlying math. Includes graded assignments and ungraded notebooks with code samples and interactive graphs.
reading.summary: The Machine Learning Specialization is a three-course beginner-friendly program created by DeepLearning.AI and Stanford Online and taught by Andrew Ng. It is a rebuilt and expanded version of the original machine learning course, redesigned to teach how machine learning works without requiring a heavy math background or deep coding experience. Finishing the program shows the ability to build effective learning algorithms and get them working on real applications.
reading.audience: The page says it is for people breaking into AI, including those with no prior math knowledge or rigorous coding background. It is also for learners who did not finish the original Machine Learning course and for those who completed it and want a fast refresher.
reading.prerequisites: No prior math knowledge or rigorous coding background is required. The math behind each algorithm is covered in optional videos that can be watched or skipped.
